verdicts.why: The brief does not decide on tiling seams, and this candidate has one. terrain.png has a dark 1 px frame on all four edges. In mean luminance the edge column/row reads 83-87 against an interior of 91.4. The wrap discontinuity is 4.0 (left-right) and 2.5 (top-bottom), against 1.3-1.5 for interior neighbours. Tiled edge to edge (tiled_2x2.png), this shows as a thin dark grid line at every join (columns and rows 1023-1024 read 83-87 against about 91 on either side), so the line will repeat across polluted ground. No lettered line (A1-F1) covers a terrain that does not tile cleanly, so I cannot REDO it, and I will not KEEP a visible seam without saying so. Everything else passes: this is our own painterly drawing, not the donor (donor_standin.png is a near-black tile grid; the candidate is warm brown mottled plaster with rust blotches); it is opaque, as a terrain must be; and the canvas is 1024x1024, not down-resolved. Secondary note, not a refusal: the candidate does not read as the sibling polluted. sibling_unpolluted.png is a cool grey (RGB about 126/129/132), fine-grained surface with low contrast (std 4.7). The candidate is warm brown (about 100/90/77) with much larger blotches (std 10.4), so on the map the boundary between polluted and clean cells will read as a different material rather than the same polymer stained. The sibling is not an owner keep, so B3 does not bind. I also measured that the sibling's left edge column is darker than its interior (115 against 129), so the seam fault may be pipeline-wide.

proposals: Terrain seam constraint: a terrain texture must tile edge to edge with no visible line at the joins, judged by eye on the 2x2 tiling. In this file's own measurements, a wrap discontinuity of about 3x the interior neighbour difference showed as a visible grid. Evidence: terrain.png has a dark 1 px frame (edge 83-87 against interior 91.4), which shows as grid lines in tiled_2x2.png. sibling_unpolluted.png also has a darkened left edge (115 against 129), so the fault may come from the generation or resize step for all terrains.

Polluted-variant constraint: a pollutedTexturePath picture reads as the same ground as its unpolluted sibling, with pollution added (stain, grime, tint), not as a different material. Evidence: sibling_unpolluted.png is cool grey with fine grain; terrain.png is warm brown with coarse painterly blotches.
Terrain inputs: the brief should say that the true-scale panel, the 32 px/cell copy and the facings do not apply to a TerrainDef, so that a terrain judge is not pushed into UNSURE: not given.

verdicts.notes: This is the check of the repairs. The first look's only blocker was the dark 1-px frame and the seam. The frame is gone: the edge columns read 89.6/89.3 and 89.6/89.6 (cols 0/1 and 1022/1023), and the edge rows read 89.4/89.4 and 89.3/89.1, against an interior of 89.2, so the edge step is about 0. In tiled_2x2.png, looked at whole and in a 512 px crop centred on the four-way join, there is no grid line and no visible seam at either join. The wrap step is gone top to bottom (1.32, against a median row step of 1.41). Left to right it is reduced but not quite at interior level: 1.98, against a median column step of 1.30 (about 1.5x), a 95th percentile of 1.50, and 1.4-1.6 on the columns beside the edge. The window reported 1.0-1.2x, which I could not reproduce. By eye this residue is invisible at full size and in the 2x2 tiling. The repair changed the 96-px border band, and I found no ghosting or doubled blotches there by eye. The band is slightly flatter than the centre (luminance std 3.76 against 4.30; adjacent-pixel detail 1.25 against 1.33). That is a mild blend-softening, and it does not read as a band in tiled_2x2.png. Everything the first look passed still holds. It is our own painterly mottled surface, not the donor's near-black tile grid (donor_standin.png). It is fully opaque (alpha min 255), as a terrain must be. It is 1024x1024, not down-resolved. No owner keep is on record, and he left no notes (subject.json). Compared with before_repair.png, the interior picture is unchanged; only the frame and border band differ.
verdicts.why: KEEP. No lettered line (A1-F1) covers tiling seams, so the small residual left-right wrap step (about 1.5x the median column step, below visibility) is recorded here and in proposals, not refused. The sibling mismatch noted on the first look still stands as a non-binding remark: sibling_unpolluted.png is a cool grey (about 126/129/132), while the candidate is a warm brown (about 100/90/77). The sibling is not an owner keep, so B3 does not bind.

proposals: Add a lettered line for terrain tiling: a terrain file must wrap with no visible seam when tiled 2x2. Advisory measure: wrap step at most about 1.2x the median adjacent-pixel step, and no edge row or column more than 2 luminance levels from the interior. Evidence: before_repair.png had a 1-px dark frame that tiled into a grid line, and nothing in A1-F1 could refuse it. After repair, terrain.png still measures a left-right wrap step of 1.98 against a 1.30 median (invisible by eye in tiled_2x2.png).

Add a terrain-sibling line: a polluted texture should read as the same material as its unpolluted sibling, stained. Evidence: sibling_unpolluted.png is cool grey (about 126/129/132, fine grain), while terrain.png is warm brown (about 100/90/77, large blotches), so a polluted/clean boundary would read as a change of material. B3 binds only owner-kept siblings, and this sibling has no keep.

Seam repairs that blend a border toward a half-shifted copy should report the band's contrast loss. Here the 96-px band measures luminance std 3.76 against 4.30 in the centre. That is not visible this time, but a wider band or a stronger blend would show as a soft frame.

The second look checked repair v1 and found it drew the old wrap seam at the midline of each border band (UNSURE on 3; measured on all 15). Repair v3 removes the frame and cross-fades the wrap without a shifted copy: measured frame <= 0.8, wrap 0.97-1.23x, worst straight line in the file and across the wrap <= 1.52x the median step (donors 1.5-8.7x), and a 2x2 tile shows no line by eye. The brief allows no third look (§When the look is enough, and when to stop), so v3 stands on its measurements. A Slime UNSURE on the second look was for the missing play-zoom input, which the brief does not define for a terrain (proposal).
